frontier.hypothesis: The whole remaining residual reduces to ONE seat question that no session has attacked directly: get the arg5 loaded VALUE into a quantity distinct from its own address register (target: address in $v0, value in $v1), which frees $v0 for the D_800A11D5 chain and — on the scaled-offset chassis, whose tail is already target-exact — removes the load-delay nop.
frontier.mechanism: s22's alignment shows the candidate coalesces arg5's load destination with its address register because the address dies at the load. Target does not coalesce, so the value survives in $v1 across insns 48-54 while the D5 chain reuses $v0 at 49-53. In C terms the anti-coalescing condition is that the ADDRESS remains live past the load — a pointer local that is read twice, or an address whose second use is the arg4 chain's base — which is a spelling nobody has tried: every banked address form uses the pointer exactly once.
frontier.next_probe: On the scaled-offset chassis (tmp/grind/CD_datasync/s22 harness, ~0.5 s/form) sweep spellings that keep an address pointer live past its own load: (a) `s32 *p5 = &tbl_125c[idx_1494[1]];` consumed as *p5 AND with p5 (or p5-derived arithmetic) reused for the arg4 base, (b) one pointer walked between the two elements (`p = &tbl_125c[idx_1494[0]]` then arg5 read through an offset of the same p), (c) both elements read through a single walking pointer with post-increment, per .claude/rules/walking-pointer-serializes-parallel-loads.md. Read every result with cmp.py 40 60 and watch specifically for the arg5 lw destination becoming a register other than its address register; the score alone will not show partial progress.

frontier.hypothesis: F32 (inherited, unchanged) — tools/ra_solver/inverse.py local can type the block-3 seat residual REACHABLE or FORECLOSED and name the C-lever vectors, converting the disposition from an exhaustion argument into a proof. s22 sharpens its input: the residual is now stated as a specific anti-coalescing condition plus target's $a0 parking of the arg4 address.
frontier.mechanism: s20's classify verdict names inverse.py as the next tool and extracted the block-3 QTYDBG attribution; find_free_reg's ascending scan means reaching $a0 requires both $v0 and $v1 occupied across the arg4 address chain's whole span at allocation time. s22 adds the second half of the spec: the arg5 value must be a separate quantity from its address, which is what keeps $v1 busy over that span.
frontier.next_probe: Run inverse.py local against CD_datasync block 3 with a HAND-VERIFIED --goal-order (perturb.py --goal-from-target still SKIPS this block: 'goal is not a topological order, 2 violations', because difflib mis-pairs the duplicate sll / lw skeletons). Bound and profile the run — the CD_ready precedent is that an unbounded inverse.py local can burn 100% CPU without finishing depth 1. A REACHABLE verdict must name a lever vector nobody has spelled; the banked count is now 103 rejected forms plus this session's 166 measured spellings.

frontier.hypothesis: The standing family trigger (inherited) — a JOINT sched.c-emission-order x global.c/local-alloc.c-seat solver closes CD_datasync, CD_sync and CD_ready together. s22 adds a new requirement for any such solver: it must be chassis-aware, because two chassis that emit identical bytes at one spelling diverge by 5 instructions one spelling away.
frontier.mechanism: Every C change that fixes the emission order breaks the register seats and vice versa — proven over 22 sessions here, 68 on CD_ready and 107 on CD_sync. The current solver suite is single-axis, which is why all three twins land on the same disposition.
frontier.next_probe: When a joint solver exists, re-open CD_datasync, CD_sync and CD_ready as ONE basin. Use the s22 harness (tmp/grind/CD_datasync/s22/, ~0.5 s/form, calibrated sandbox = lev + nop - 3, now with declaration-block rewriting and three parameterised form generators) as the scoring loop, and run every candidate lever on BOTH the wrapper and the duplicated-arms chassis rather than assuming they agree.
